questions.q: What is the main function of the sepal in a flower?
questions.answer: To protect the flower bud
questions.explain: The sepal protects the flower while it is still a bud.
procedure: The sepal is the green, leaf-like part at the base of the flower
While the flower is still a bud, the sepal wraps around it
This protects the delicate inner parts from damage and weather
Once the flower opens, the sepal stays at the base
Answer: To protect the flower bud

questions.q: What is the coloured part of a flower called?
questions.answer: Petal
questions.explain: Petals are the bright, coloured parts of a flower.
procedure: Look at any flower — the colourful leaves you see are petals
Petals are usually bright and attractive
Their colour and scent attract insects and birds
Answer: Petal

questions.q: Which part of a flower produces pollen?
questions.answer: Stamen
questions.explain: The stamen is the male part of the flower and produces pollen.
procedure: The stamen is the male part of the flower
It has two parts: the anther and the filament
The anther at the top produces the yellow pollen grains
Answer: Stamen

questions.q: Which part of the flower receives pollen during pollination?
questions.answer: Stigma
questions.explain: The stigma is the top of the pistil and receives pollen grains.
procedure: The pistil is the female part of the flower
Its top is called the stigma
The stigma is sticky, so pollen grains stick to it
Answer: Stigma

questions.q: What is the male part of a flower called?
questions.answer: Stamen
questions.explain: The stamen is the male part of a flower.
procedure: Flowers have both male and female parts
The male part is called the stamen
It produces pollen, which contains the male sex cells
Answer: Stamen

questions.q: What is the female part of a flower called?
questions.answer: Pistil
questions.explain: The pistil is the female part of a flower.
procedure: The female part of a flower is the pistil
It has three parts: stigma, style, and ovary
The ovary contains the egg cells (ovules)
Answer: Pistil

questions.q: Which part of the pistil contains the egg cells?
questions.answer: Ovary
questions.explain: The ovary is at the base of the pistil and contains the egg cells.
procedure: The pistil has three parts: stigma (top), style (middle), and ovary (bottom)
The ovary is the swollen base of the pistil
Inside the ovary are the ovules (egg cells)
After fertilization, the ovary becomes the fruit
Answer: Ovary

questions.q: What is the transfer of pollen from the anther to the stigma called?
questions.answer: Pollination
questions.explain: Pollination is the transfer of pollen to the stigma.
procedure: Pollination = movement of pollen from anther to stigma
It can happen within the same flower or between flowers
Wind, insects, birds, and water can carry pollen
Answer: Pollination

questions.q: After pollination, what happens to the pollen grain on the stigma?
options: It grows a tube down to the ovary
questions.answer: It grows a tube down to the ovary
questions.explain: The pollen grain grows a pollen tube down through the style to reach the ovary.
procedure: A pollen grain lands on the sticky stigma
It grows a long tube called the pollen tube
The tube grows down through the style to the ovary
The male sex cell travels down the tube to join the egg cell
Answer: It grows a tube down to the ovary

questions.q: What is formed when the male and female sex cells join?
questions.answer: A seed
questions.explain: The joining of male and female cells forms a seed.
procedure: Fertilization = when male and female cells join
The fertilized egg cell develops into a seed
The ovary around it becomes the fruit
Answer: A seed

questions.q: Which part of the flower becomes the fruit after fertilization?
questions.answer: The ovary
questions.explain: After fertilization, the ovary grows into the fruit.
procedure: Before fertilization: the ovary holds the ovules (egg cells)
After fertilization: the ovules become seeds
The ovary itself grows and becomes the fruit
This is why every fruit contains seeds
Answer: The ovary

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a part of the stamen?
questions.answer: Stigma
questions.explain: The stigma is part of the pistil, not the stamen.
procedure: Stamen = anther + filament (male parts)
Pistil = stigma + style + ovary (female parts)
The stigma belongs to the pistil, not the stamen
Answer: Stigma

questions.q: What is the stalk that supports the anther called?
questions.answer: Filament
questions.explain: The filament is the thin stalk that holds up the anther.
procedure: The stamen has two parts: anther and filament
The anther is at the top — it holds pollen
The filament is the thin stalk that supports the anther
Answer: Filament

questions.q: What is the stalk that supports the stigma called?
questions.answer: Style
questions.explain: The style is the tube that connects the stigma to the ovary.
procedure: The pistil has three parts: stigma, style, ovary
The stigma is at the top
The style is the middle tube that connects stigma to ovary
Answer: Style

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a way pollen can be transferred?
questions.answer: Electricity
questions.explain: Pollen is transferred by wind, insects, birds, or water — not electricity.
procedure: Pollination happens through natural agents
Wind carries light pollen grains
Insects and birds carry pollen as they visit flowers
Water can carry pollen in some water plants
Electricity is not a pollinating agent
Answer: Electricity

questions.q: Why are petals usually brightly coloured?
options: To make the flower look nice for humans
To attract insects and birds for pollination
To protect the flower from rain
To help the flower grow taller
questions.answer: To attract insects and birds for pollination
questions.explain: Bright petals attract pollinators, which help the flower reproduce.
procedure: Many flowers need insects or birds to carry pollen
Bright colours and pleasant scents attract these pollinators
The pollinators come for nectar, but leave with pollen on their bodies
They carry the pollen to the next flower
Answer: To attract insects and birds for pollination

questions.q: Which part of the flower is usually green and found at the base?
questions.answer: Sepal
questions.explain: The sepal is the green, leaf-like part at the base of the flower.
procedure: Look at a flower from the outside
The green, leaf-like parts at the bottom are sepals
They protect the flower bud before it opens
Answer: Sepal

questions.q: What do flowers produce that we often enjoy for their beauty and smell?
questions.answer: Nectar and scent
questions.explain: Flowers produce nectar and scent that attract pollinators.
procedure: Flowers make nectar (a sweet liquid) inside them
They also release scent through their petals
Both are used to attract insects and birds
Nectar also provides food for the pollinators
Answer: Nectar and scent

questions.q: A bee visits a flower and later visits another. What is the bee doing?
questions.answer: Pollinating the flowers
questions.explain: The bee carries pollen from one flower to another.
procedure: As a bee collects nectar, pollen sticks to its hairy body
When it visits the next flower, some of that pollen rubs off onto the stigma
This transfer is called pollination
The bee is helping the flowers reproduce
Answer: Pollinating the flowers

questions.q: Which of the following is the correct order of the flower's life from bud to seed?
options: Bud → Flower → Pollination → Fertilization → Fruit and Seed
questions.answer: Bud → Flower → Pollination → Fertilization → Fruit and Seed
questions.explain: The flower grows from a bud, opens, gets pollinated, fertilized, and produces fruit and seeds.
procedure: 1. Bud forms (protected by sepals)
2. Bud opens into a flower with petals
3. Pollination happens (pollen reaches stigma)
4. Fertilization happens (sex cells join)
5. Ovary becomes fruit, ovules become seeds
Answer: Bud → Flower → Pollination → Fertilization → Fruit and Seed

questions.q: What is the water cycle?
options: Water moving through pipes in a house
The continuous movement of water between land, sea, and air
questions.answer: The continuous movement of water between land, sea, and air
questions.explain: The water cycle is the never-ending movement of water on Earth.
procedure: The water cycle is also called the hydrological cycle
Water moves between the oceans, the sky, and the land
It changes form: liquid → gas → liquid
This movement never stops
Answer: The continuous movement of water between land, sea, and air

questions.q: What is it called when water changes from liquid to gas?
questions.answer: Evaporation
questions.explain: Evaporation is when water changes from liquid to gas (water vapour).
procedure: The sun heats water in oceans, rivers, and lakes
When water is heated enough, it changes into water vapour (a gas)
This process is called evaporation
You can see it when puddles dry up on a hot day
Answer: Evaporation

questions.q: What is the main source of energy that drives the water cycle?
questions.answer: The sun
questions.explain: The sun provides the heat energy that powers the water cycle.
procedure: The water cycle needs energy to keep going
That energy comes from the sun
The sun heats water in oceans, lakes, and rivers
This causes evaporation to happen
Answer: The sun

questions.q: What is it called when water vapour cools and turns back into liquid?
questions.answer: Condensation
questions.explain: Condensation is when water vapour cools and becomes liquid water.
procedure: Water vapour rises into the sky
As it goes higher, the air is colder
The cool air makes the water vapour turn back into tiny droplets
This process is called condensation
Answer: Condensation

questions.q: What do we call the tiny water droplets that form in the sky?
questions.answer: Clouds
questions.explain: Clouds are made of tiny water droplets that form from condensation.
procedure: When water vapour condenses high in the sky, it forms tiny droplets
Millions of these droplets together form clouds
Clouds look white or grey depending on the light and thickness
Answer: Clouds

questions.q: What is it called when water falls from clouds as rain, hail, or snow?
questions.answer: Precipitation
questions.explain: Precipitation is water falling from clouds to the ground.
procedure: Cloud droplets grow bigger and heavier
When they become too heavy, they fall as precipitation
Precipitation can be rain, hail, or snow
Answer: Precipitation

questions.q: What is transpiration?
options: Water moving from soil to plant roots
Water vapour released from plant leaves into the air
questions.answer: Water vapour released from plant leaves into the air
questions.explain: Transpiration is the release of water vapour from plants.
procedure: Plants take in water through their roots
Some of this water travels up to the leaves
The leaves release extra water as vapour into the air
This release is called transpiration
Answer: Water vapour released from plant leaves into the air

questions.q: Which of these is NOT part of the water cycle?
questions.answer: Electricity
questions.explain: Electricity is not part of the water cycle.
procedure: The main stages of the water cycle are: evaporation, condensation, precipitation, and collection
Transpiration is also part of the cycle
Electricity is not involved in the water cycle
Answer: Electricity

questions.q: Where does the water that falls as rain go?
options: It is soaked into the ground or flows into rivers and lakes
questions.answer: It is soaked into the ground or flows into rivers and lakes
questions.explain: Rainwater is collected in the ground, rivers, lakes, and oceans.
procedure: When rain falls, some water sinks into the ground
Some water flows over the land into streams and rivers
Rivers carry the water into lakes and oceans
This step is called collection
Answer: It is soaked into the ground or flows into rivers and lakes

questions.q: Why is the water cycle important for life on Earth?
options: It makes the sky look pretty
It continuously supplies fresh water for plants, animals, and humans
questions.answer: It continuously supplies fresh water for plants, animals, and humans
questions.explain: The water cycle gives us a constant supply of fresh water.
procedure: All living things need water
The water cycle moves water from the oceans to the land as rain
Plants, animals, and humans use this fresh water
The cycle keeps repeating, so water is never used up
Answer: It continuously supplies fresh water for plants, animals, and humans

questions.q: Which state of matter is water vapour?
questions.answer: Gas
questions.explain: Water vapour is water in its gas form.
procedure: Water can exist in three states: solid (ice), liquid (water), gas (vapour)
Water vapour is the gas form of water
It is invisible — you cannot see water vapour directly
Answer: Gas

questions.q: When you boil water in a pot, what do you see rising?
questions.answer: Steam (water vapour)
questions.explain: Steam rises when water is heated — that's water vapour.
procedure: When water is heated, it changes into gas
The gas rises as steam
The white mist you see is actually tiny water droplets that form when steam hits cooler air
This is a real-life example of evaporation and condensation
Answer: Steam (water vapour)

questions.q: Why does wet ground dry up faster on a sunny day?
options: Because the sun drinks the water
Because the heat makes water evaporate faster
Because wind blows the water away
questions.answer: Because the heat makes water evaporate faster
questions.explain: Heat from the sun speeds up evaporation.
procedure: Evaporation happens all the time, but faster when it's hot
The sun heats the wet ground
The heat gives water molecules energy to escape as vapour
So the water dries up faster on a sunny day
Answer: Because the heat makes water evaporate faster

questions.q: Where does most evaporation happen on Earth?
questions.answer: In the oceans
questions.explain: Oceans cover most of Earth, so most evaporation happens there.
procedure: Oceans cover about 71% of Earth's surface
Because they are so large, most evaporation happens there
The sun heats the ocean surface, causing water to turn into vapour
Answer: In the oceans

questions.q: What causes rain to fall from clouds?
options: The clouds open up like doors
Water droplets in clouds get too heavy and fall
The moon pulls the rain down
questions.answer: Water droplets in clouds get too heavy and fall
questions.explain: When cloud droplets combine and become heavy, they fall as rain.
procedure: Clouds are made of tiny water droplets
Droplets bump into each other and join together
They grow bigger and heavier
When they become too heavy to float, they fall as rain
Answer: Water droplets in clouds get too heavy and fall

questions.q: Which process returns water to the sky from plants?
questions.answer: Transpiration
questions.explain: Transpiration is the release of water vapour from plant leaves.
procedure: Plants absorb water through their roots
Some water is used for food-making (photosynthesis)
The rest is released as vapour through small holes in the leaves
This release is called transpiration
Answer: Transpiration

questions.q: If we cut down too many trees, how does it affect the water cycle?
options: Less transpiration happens, which can affect rainfall patterns
questions.answer: Less transpiration happens, which can affect rainfall patterns
questions.explain: Fewer trees means less transpiration and less moisture in the air.
procedure: Trees release water vapour into the air through transpiration
This vapour helps form clouds and rain
When many trees are cut down, less vapour is released
This can lead to less rainfall in the area
Answer: Less transpiration happens, which can affect rainfall patterns

questions.q: Which of these is a good way to conserve water?
options: Use a bucket instead of a hose when washing a car
questions.answer: Use a bucket instead of a hose when washing a car
questions.explain: Using a bucket uses much less water than a running hose.
procedure: Water conservation means using less water
A hose can waste many litres per minute
A bucket uses only a few litres total
Small choices save a lot of water over time
Answer: Use a bucket instead of a hose when washing a car

questions.q: What happens to water when it freezes?
questions.answer: It becomes a solid (ice)
questions.explain: When water freezes, it becomes solid ice.
procedure: Water exists in three states: solid, liquid, gas
When water cools below 0°C, it freezes
It becomes solid ice
When it warms up again, it melts back to liquid water
Answer: It becomes a solid (ice)

questions.q: Which of the following is a real-life example of condensation?
options: Water droplets on the outside of a cold glass
questions.answer: Water droplets on the outside of a cold glass
questions.explain: Water vapour in the air cools on the cold glass and turns into droplets.
procedure: A cold glass makes the air around it cool
Water vapour in the air touches the cold glass
The vapour cools and turns into liquid droplets
This is condensation — the same process that forms clouds
Answer: Water droplets on the outside of a cold glass

questions.q: What is the main job of the digestive system?
options: To pump blood around the body
To break down food so the body can use it
questions.answer: To break down food so the body can use it
questions.explain: The digestive system breaks down food into nutrients the body can absorb.
procedure: Food enters the body through the mouth
It travels through the digestive system
The body breaks it down into nutrients
These nutrients are absorbed and used for energy and growth
Answer: To break down food so the body can use it

questions.q: Where does digestion begin?
questions.answer: In the mouth
questions.explain: Digestion begins in the mouth where teeth chew food and saliva starts breaking it down.
procedure: Food enters the mouth first
Teeth chew and grind the food into smaller pieces
Saliva mixes with the food and starts breaking it down
Then the food is swallowed
Answer: In the mouth

questions.q: What is the oesophagus?
options: A tube that carries food from the mouth to the stomach
The organ that helps us breathe
The bone that protects the heart
questions.answer: A tube that carries food from the mouth to the stomach
questions.explain: The oesophagus is the food pipe connecting the mouth to the stomach.
procedure: After swallowing, food travels down the oesophagus
The oesophagus is also called the food pipe
It connects the mouth to the stomach
Muscles push the food down to the stomach
Answer: A tube that carries food from the mouth to the stomach

questions.q: What happens to food inside the stomach?
options: It is churned and mixed with digestive juices
It is sent directly to the heart
questions.answer: It is churned and mixed with digestive juices
questions.explain: The stomach churns food and mixes it with juices that break it down further.
procedure: Food arrives in the stomach from the oesophagus
The stomach muscles churn the food
Digestive juices mix with the food
The food becomes a thick liquid before moving on
Answer: It is churned and mixed with digestive juices

questions.q: Where are most nutrients absorbed into the body?
questions.answer: In the small intestine
questions.explain: Most nutrients are absorbed into the blood in the small intestine.
procedure: After the stomach, food moves into the small intestine
The small intestine is long and coiled
Its walls absorb nutrients from the food
These nutrients enter the blood and go to the body
Answer: In the small intestine

questions.q: What is the main job of the large intestine?
options: To absorb water from what is left
questions.answer: To absorb water from what is left
questions.explain: The large intestine absorbs water and forms solid waste.
procedure: After the small intestine, what is left moves to the large intestine
The large intestine absorbs water from it
The remaining waste becomes solid
It is then removed from the body
Answer: To absorb water from what is left

questions.q: What is digestion?
options: The process of breaking down food into nutrients
questions.answer: The process of breaking down food into nutrients
questions.explain: Digestion is how the body breaks food into useful nutrients.
procedure: Food must be broken down to be useful
This happens through chewing, churning, and digestive juices
The food becomes nutrients small enough to absorb
This whole process is called digestion
Answer: The process of breaking down food into nutrients

questions.q: What is the main job of the heart?
options: To pump blood around the body
questions.answer: To pump blood around the body
questions.explain: The heart pumps blood that carries oxygen and nutrients to every part of the body.
procedure: The heart is a strong muscle in the chest
It pumps blood through tubes called blood vessels
Blood carries oxygen and nutrients
These reach every part of the body
Answer: To pump blood around the body

questions.q: What is the circulatory system?
options: The heart, blood, and blood vessels working together
questions.answer: The heart, blood, and blood vessels working together
questions.explain: The circulatory system moves blood around the body.
procedure: The circulatory system includes the heart, blood, and blood vessels
The heart pumps the blood
Blood vessels are the tubes that carry the blood
Together they move blood around the body
Answer: The heart, blood, and blood vessels working together

questions.q: What do arteries and veins do?
options: They carry food to the stomach
They carry blood around the body
questions.answer: They carry blood around the body
questions.explain: Arteries and veins are blood vessels that carry blood.
procedure: Blood vessels are tubes that carry blood
Arteries carry blood away from the heart
Veins carry blood back to the heart
Together they carry blood all around the body
Answer: They carry blood around the body

questions.q: What is circulation?
options: The movement of blood around the body
The movement of food through the body
The movement of air into the lungs
The movement of bones at a joint
questions.answer: The movement of blood around the body
questions.explain: Circulation is the continuous movement of blood through the body.
procedure: The heart pumps blood
Blood travels through blood vessels
It delivers oxygen and nutrients to the body
Then it returns to the heart and repeats
This continuous movement is called circulation
Answer: The movement of blood around the body

questions.q: Where does air enter the body?
questions.answer: Through the nose and mouth
questions.explain: Air enters the body through the nose or mouth.
procedure: We breathe in air through the nose or mouth
The nose filters and warms the air
The air then travels down the windpipe
It eventually reaches the lungs
Answer: Through the nose and mouth

questions.q: What is the windpipe?
options: A tube that carries air from the throat to the lungs
A tube that carries food to the stomach
questions.answer: A tube that carries air from the throat to the lungs
questions.explain: The windpipe (trachea) carries air from the throat to the lungs.
procedure: After entering the nose or mouth, air goes into the windpipe
The windpipe is also called the trachea
It is a tube that leads down to the lungs
Air passes through it with every breath
Answer: A tube that carries air from the throat to the lungs

questions.q: What happens inside the lungs?
options: Oxygen from the air enters the blood
questions.answer: Oxygen from the air enters the blood
questions.explain: In the lungs, oxygen passes into the blood and carbon dioxide leaves it.
procedure: Air reaches the lungs through the windpipe
Inside the lungs, air fills tiny air sacs
Oxygen from the air passes into the blood
At the same time, carbon dioxide leaves the blood to be breathed out
Answer: Oxygen from the air enters the blood

questions.q: Why do we need to breathe?
options: To get oxygen into the body and remove carbon dioxide
questions.answer: To get oxygen into the body and remove carbon dioxide
questions.explain: Breathing brings in oxygen and removes carbon dioxide.
procedure: Every cell in the body needs oxygen
Oxygen comes from the air we breathe in
The body also makes carbon dioxide as waste
Breathing out removes carbon dioxide
Answer: To get oxygen into the body and remove carbon dioxide

questions.q: What is the skeleton for?
options: To support the body, protect organs, and help it move
questions.answer: To support the body, protect organs, and help it move
questions.explain: The skeleton supports the body, protects organs, and works with muscles for movement.
procedure: The skeleton is made of bones
Bones support the body and give it shape
They protect important organs — like the skull protects the brain and the ribs protect the heart
Muscles pull on bones to help us move
Answer: To support the body, protect organs, and help it move

questions.q: What is a joint?
options: A place where two bones meet
questions.answer: A place where two bones meet
questions.explain: A joint is where two bones meet and allow movement.
procedure: Bones join together at joints
Joints allow the bones to move
The knee, elbow, shoulder, and neck all have joints
Without joints, the body could not bend or move
Answer: A place where two bones meet

questions.q: Which of these is a type of joint?
questions.answer: Ball-and-socket joint
questions.explain: Ball-and-socket is one of the main types of joints in the body.
procedure: There are several types of joints in the body
Ball-and-socket joints — like at the shoulder — allow movement in all directions
Hinge joints — like the knee — allow back-and-forth movement
Pivot joints — like the neck — allow turning
Answer: Ball-and-socket joint

questions.q: What does the brain do?
options: It controls the whole body and helps us think
questions.answer: It controls the whole body and helps us think
questions.explain: The brain is the control centre of the body — it directs everything we do.
procedure: The brain is inside the skull
It sends messages through nerves to every part of the body
It controls movement, breathing, thinking, and feeling
It is the control centre of the whole body
Answer: It controls the whole body and helps us think

questions.q: How do the body systems work together?
options: They work alone and never help each other
They work as a team to keep the body alive and healthy
Only one system works at a time
They only work when we sleep
questions.answer: They work as a team to keep the body alive and healthy
questions.explain: The body systems work together — for example, the digestive system provides nutrients that the circulatory system delivers to every cell.
procedure: Each body system has its own job
But no system works alone
The digestive system provides nutrients
The circulatory system carries them around
The respiratory system brings in oxygen
The nervous system controls everything
Together they keep the body alive and healthy
Answer: They work as a team to keep the body alive and healthy

questions.q: What is kinetic energy?
questions.answer: Energy of movement
questions.explain: Kinetic energy is the energy an object has because it is moving.
procedure: Kinetic comes from the Greek word for 'motion'
Anything that moves has kinetic energy
The faster it moves, the more kinetic energy it has
Answer: Energy of movement

questions.q: Which of these shows kinetic energy?
options: A ball sitting on the ground
questions.answer: A child running
questions.explain: Running is movement, so a running child has kinetic energy.
procedure: Kinetic energy = energy of movement
A child running is moving — so they have kinetic energy
A ball on the ground, a book on a shelf, and a parked car are all still
Answer: A child running

questions.q: What is potential energy?
options: Stored energy waiting to be used
questions.answer: Stored energy waiting to be used
questions.explain: Potential energy is energy that is stored and ready to be released.
procedure: Potential energy is stored energy
It is waiting to be used or released
A ball on a hill has potential energy — it can roll down
Answer: Stored energy waiting to be used

questions.q: Which of these shows potential energy?
options: A ball rolling down a hill
A ball at the top of a hill
questions.answer: A ball at the top of a hill
questions.explain: A ball at the top of a hill is not moving yet — it has stored (potential) energy.
procedure: A ball at the top of a hill has not started moving yet
But it has stored energy ready to be released
This stored energy is potential energy
Once it starts rolling, the potential energy becomes kinetic energy
Answer: A ball at the top of a hill

questions.q: What is heat energy?
options: Energy from warm or hot objects
questions.answer: Energy from warm or hot objects
questions.explain: Heat energy comes from warm or hot objects and makes things warmer.
procedure: Heat is a form of energy
Warm or hot objects give off heat energy
Heat makes things warmer
Answer: Energy from warm or hot objects

questions.q: Which of these is a source of heat energy?
questions.answer: A fire
questions.explain: Fire produces heat energy.
procedure: Heat energy comes from warm or hot objects
A fire is very hot — it gives off lots of heat energy
A book, mirror, and stone at room temperature do not produce noticeable heat
Answer: A fire

questions.q: What is light energy?
questions.answer: Energy that we can see
questions.explain: Light energy is the energy we can see with our eyes.
procedure: Light is a form of energy
We can see it with our eyes
It comes from sources like the sun, bulbs, and candles
Answer: Energy that we can see

questions.q: Which of these is a source of light energy?
questions.answer: The sun
questions.explain: The sun is our main natural source of light.
procedure: Light energy comes from light sources
The sun is the biggest natural light source
Other sources include torches, bulbs, and candles
Answer: The sun

questions.q: What is sound energy?
questions.answer: Energy we can hear
questions.explain: Sound energy is the energy we hear — produced by vibrations.
procedure: Sound is a form of energy
It is made when something vibrates
Our ears pick up these vibrations as sound
Answer: Energy we can hear

questions.q: Which of these produces sound energy?
questions.answer: A drum being beaten
questions.explain: A drum vibrates when beaten, producing sound energy.
procedure: Sound is made when something vibrates
When a drum is beaten, the skin vibrates
These vibrations travel through the air as sound
Answer: A drum being beaten

questions.q: What is electrical energy?
options: Energy that flows as electric current
questions.answer: Energy that flows as electric current
questions.explain: Electrical energy is carried by moving electric charges (current).
procedure: Electrical energy is carried by electric current
It flows through wires and circuits
Batteries and sockets are sources of electrical energy
Answer: Energy that flows as electric current

questions.q: Which of these is a source of electrical energy?
questions.answer: A battery
questions.explain: A battery stores chemical energy that can become electrical energy.
procedure: A battery stores energy inside it
When connected in a circuit, it releases electrical energy
Other sources include power sockets and generators
Answer: A battery

questions.q: What is chemical energy?
options: Energy stored in substances like food and fuel
questions.answer: Energy stored in substances like food and fuel
questions.explain: Chemical energy is stored in the bonds of substances like food and fuel.
procedure: Chemical energy is stored inside substances
Food contains chemical energy we use when we eat
Fuel contains chemical energy that is released when it burns
Answer: Energy stored in substances like food and fuel

questions.q: Where is chemical energy stored in our body?
questions.answer: In the food we eat
questions.explain: Food contains chemical energy that our body uses.
procedure: The food we eat contains chemical energy
Our body breaks it down and releases the energy
We use this energy to move, think, and grow
Answer: In the food we eat

questions.q: What is energy conversion?
options: When energy changes from one form to another
questions.answer: When energy changes from one form to another
questions.explain: Energy conversion is when energy changes form — like electrical energy becoming light.
procedure: Energy can change from one form to another
